Champion browse by type eq/excite/filter/wah wah wah fuzz-wah browse by enclosure treadle B&M Champion Wah Fuzz Published on November 13, 2010 Champion fuzz-wah foot-controlled treadle Information The B&M Champion Wah Fuzz is a dual-function vintage effects pedal produced in the late 1970s for Barnes & Mullins by Sola Sound in England. It combines the classic Colorsound-style wah circuit with a powerful fuzz section derived from the Jumbo Tone Bender design, creating a unit capable of both smooth filter sweeps and heavy, sustaining distortion. Sharing its circuit lineage with other private-label Sola Sound builds such as the CSL, G.B., R.K.I., and West Wood variants, the Champion Wah Fuzz delivers the characteristic Colorsound tone - broad sweep, rich harmonics, and aggressive fuzz texture. The pedal features independent footswitches allowing the fuzz and wah sections to be activated separately or together. The wah section provides a long, vocal sweep with a throaty response, while the fuzz circuit produces dense, saturated tones with pronounced low-end and sustain suitable for both guitar and bass. Inside, the circuit includes three internal trimpots for fine-tuning fuzz level, tone, and sustain, offering additional control over its dynamic range and texture. Like many Sola Sound designs from this era, the enclosure is built from cast metal with a rocker treadle format and mechanical footswitches. The B&M Champion Wah Fuzz remains notable for its raw, unrefined tone and the ability to toggle between wah-only, fuzz-only, or combined fuzz-wah operation, making it one of the more versatile and collectible British pedals of its class. Controls Footswitches: Independent on/off control for Wah and Fuzz sections. Wah treadle: Sweeps the filter frequency for the wah effect. Internal trimpots: Adjust fuzz volume, tone, and sustain. Connections Input: 1/4" instrument input. Output: 1/4" audio output. Power: 9V battery (some modified units feature 9V DC input). Technical Specifications Circuit type: Combined Colorsound wah and Jumbo Tone Bender-style fuzz Operation: Independent or combined Fuzz and Wah modes Inductor: Siemens inductor (typical for Colorsound builds of the period) Power source: 9V battery (some later modifications with DC input) Construction: Cast metal treadle encl
